newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia state to crack down on indecent dressing.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia state to crack down on indecent dressing.

text.p: Religious authorities in Malaysia's central Selangor state say they will crack down on Moslems who dress indecently in public.

"We will only detain those who go beyond the limit, like the case of the three women who took part in the beauty pageant," Selangor Religious Department Director Nahwari Hashim was quoted as saying in The Star newspaper on Thursday.
He was referring to three Moslem women who were rounded up last month by religious authorities after parading in bathing suits in the Miss Malaysia Petite competition.
According to the Selangor religious body, Moslem women who wear body-hugging dresses, bikinis, low-cut blouses and high-slit skirts can be charged.
Moslem men can be prosecuted if they appear in public showing off the parts of the body between the navel and the thighs.
The women who participated in the pageant are aged between 18 and 23, and if convicted are each liable for a maximum fine of 1,000 ringgit ($200) or six months' jail or both.
On Wednesday, the Shah Alam Sharia Court rejected the women's application to have the charges against them withdrawn.
The Selangor Religious Department has so far detained 2,763 people for both "dressing and acting indecently in public", the newspaper reported.
While Malaysia's federal government operates under secular laws, more than half of its multi-ethnic 21 million citizens are Moslem, and certain states like Selangor adhere closely to the religion.
Last year, religious leaders in Selangor state were in the spotlight when they banned pop superstar Michael Jackson from holding a concert in Shah Alam, the state's capital.
They expressed concerns that the U.S. singer, who has faced child molestation charges and is known for crotch-grabbing antics during his performances, would corrupt the morals of Malaysia's youth.
The concert was eventually staged at a stadium in Kuala Lumpur, which is part of the federal territory and outside of Selangor state's jurisdiction.
